title: Consecutive levels of a coherent formal module have equal support
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I an ideal sheaf, and F a coherent formal module. For every n ≥ 0, the support of F at level n+1 equals the support at level n.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV, first sentence of proof of (1)

proof.text: At x put M = (F at op (n+1))_x and let J be the stalk ideal. Apply ideal_module_product_stalk to identify the stalk of its quotient by I^(n+1) with M/(J^(n+1)M), then use the quotient isomorphism in the formal-system conditions to identify this with (F at op n)_x. The annihilation condition at op (n+1), mapped by the zero-morphism-preserving stalk functor, gives J^(n+2)M = 0 via the product-range identification. If M = 0 its quotient is zero. Conversely a zero quotient gives J^(n+1)M = M. Applying J^(n+1) once more gives J^(2(n+1))M = M. Since 2(n+1) >= n+2, ideal-power antitonicity gives M = 0. Negating the resulting equivalence of stalk subsingleton predicates and set extensionality prove the support equality.

lean.statement: theorem formalModule_support_succ {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) (n : ℕ) : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((F.obj.obj (op (n + 1))).presheaf.stalk x)} = {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((F.obj.obj (op n)).presheaf.stalk x)}
